findings.title: SQL expression feature flag is ignored; helper always returns false
findings.body: In `enableSqlExpressions`, `enabled` is assigned `!h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`, but both the `if` branch and the fall-through return `false`. The function therefore always returns false regardless of `featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions`. As a result `ReadQuery` rejects every SQL expression with `sqlExpressions is not implemented`, and enabling the documented `sqlExpressions` feature flag has no effect. If hard-disabling is intended, remove the flag check and update the flag documentation; otherwise return `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`.

findings.title: Stub DB makes TablesList/NewSQLCommand fail with misleading invalid-SQL error
findings.body: All methods on the new in-memory DB return `not implemented`, but `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` still calls `RunCommands` from `TablesList`. Thus `TablesList` can never parse any SQL and `NewSQLCommand` always returns `sql-invalid-sql` with the public message `error reading SQL command` for any non-empty SQL expression. That also affects the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand` path, which is not guarded by the new reader check, and produces a misleading 400 rather than a clear feature-disabled error. Either remove the SQL command/parser code path entirely or make the disabled state explicit at command construction.

findings.title: No test covers disabled SQL expressions even when the feature flag is enabled
findings.body: The security fix relies on the new `enableSqlExpressions` gate, but no test is added to assert that a `QueryTypeSQL` query is rejected and that the feature flag cannot re-enable it. A test with `FlagSqlExpressions` enabled would have caught the helper's always-false behavior and will help prevent a future regression that reopens the RCE/LFI path.
